answer: Requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can vote or claim rewards makes fake identities expensive: one operator must fund every Sybil separately, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Like an ember that only stays alive while fed, reputation should also age slowly, so a newly created haven for spam cannot instantly gain trust. A comet-like burst of many fresh accounts therefore looks suspicious, and the attacker pays real capital and waiting time for each identity instead of creating them free.
